status: Door and stone refinement, interpolated character motion and visibility optimization validated in representative desktop views
browser: Codex in-app Chromium: revised surfaces rendered in WebGPU and WebGL development previews. Final production pass selected WebGL 2 and validated the single-pass shader warmup.
observations: Satin bronze constant colour restored with source procedural noise baked separately at 2048 square, physical six-micrometre height and source roughness range.
Original 840-square cream stone image retained byte-for-byte; albedo repeat deliberately changed from 4.8 to 1.2 metres. No source texture resolution reduced.
Warm 12-degree sun and existing matched sunset GI/reflection captures retained. Door and studio reference views were visually inspected in the final production build.
Actual controller and Rapier walking/body-camera displacement stayed within 3 percent of expected at 60, 90, 144 and 165 Hz; original staircase and seating tests still pass.
Nine static meshes partitioned into 70 index-only cells, preserving all triangles and shared vertex attributes/materials. Full-source reference-frustum counts are attached.
Moving character keeps a stable material shader across room boundaries; redundant screen-output shader compilation removed.
Production preload reaches Explore/Cinematic, cinematic runs and pauses, exploration handoff and body-camera toggle work in the inspected browser.

console.development_issue_resolved: One simultaneous development asset load reported a generic network error; the normal Retry action completed successfully. All 100 production dependencies subsequently passed HTTP and byte-length checks.

limits: Frustum triangle reductions are not measured GPU-time gains; additional cells increase draw calls. No sustained GPU benchmark or mobile qualification was performed.
Original stone image has limited native resolution. Small lightmap seams and coarse captured reflections can remain visible; this is not an artifact-free Cycles match.
Temporal reconstruction can soften fine lines or leave transient disocclusion trails. Numerical movement tests do not prove zero frame-pacing jitter on every GPU.
The full detailed asset set remains resident. Architecture GI is ray traced offline; reflections use static captures, not browser hardware ray tracing.
Vercel deployment and domain connection remain unconfigured.
